HOW IT WORKS

Understand the model.

Three connected parts: charging activity, company participation and your weekly account illustration.

Try the operating model.

Change charging activity and electricity costs. See a surplus or a shortfall.

Inside a charging station
OPERATING ACTIVITY

A driver pays for a charging session.

In the proposed model, charging fees generate business revenue. Electricity, equipment, site costs and other expenses would be deducted before any distributable proceeds are known.

Charging payments − operating costs
The demo is not connected to station payment or operating data.
FOLLOW THE MONEY

From a charging session
to a possible distribution.

Revenue is the starting point. The business must cover its costs before a distribution can be considered.

  1. 01

    Charging receipts

    Drivers pay for electricity and charging service.

  2. 02

    Operating costs

    Electricity, site costs, service and reserves.

  3. 03

    Business result

    The amount remaining after the example costs.

  4. 04

    Distribution rules

    Company and client rights determine any payout.

TEACHING EXAMPLE · ONE WEEK

What if charging activity changes?

Invented round numbers to explain costs. These are not station results, forecasts or the basis of a plan rate.

In this illustration, electricity changes with receipts. Site, service and reserve amounts stay fixed. Real costs may behave differently.

Charging receipts
$1,000.00
Electricity
−$350.00
Site costs
−$150.00
Service & operations
−$120.00
Reserve allowance
−$80.00
Balance after example costsBefore tax and distribution rules
$300.00

The $300 balance is not a client payout. Company and client distribution rules are not defined.

The 43% assumption is not applied here: its scope and entitlement to profits are unverified. A fixed weekly rate cannot be inferred from this example.

TWO DIFFERENT PARTS OF THE MODEL

Company participation.
Your client plan.

A company interest and the terms offered to a client are different things. Each needs its own documented basis.

43%

Company participation assumption

A proposed interest in a network. Its scope and ownership documents are not verified. It does not mean 43% of US charging stations.

Your plan

A calculation inside your account

Your station group sets the demo rate. You choose the amount, and the account calculates the weekly illustration. It is not derived from the performance of the public stations shown.
